title: Your Greek values
line: Fifteen Greek values, two at a time: which matter most to you?
intro: For Athena, “ancient” is not a date but a quality: a being’s position towards the ἀρχαί, the value principles. Here are fifteen Greek values, each with Athena’s reading of it. Compare them two at a time, and find the five that matter most to you.
does: Compare fifteen Greek values two at a time, and find your five.
trains: Knowing what you truly value, through the Greek words for it.
later: Claude could read your five with your answers and say what Athena’s teaching adds to each.

values.name: Virtue
values.means: Athena reads it as “ever-flowing” (ἀεὶ ῥεῖν): the soul’s energy flowing freely, without blockages.

values.name: Wisdom
values.means: Living awareness in touch with the here and now, where life itself tells you what is what.

values.name: Practical wisdom
values.means: In Athena’s etymology, understanding of motion and flow: the mind moving rightly with what happens.

values.name: Justice
values.means: Not getting your rights but balance held from the middle, each part of the soul doing its own.

values.name: Courage
values.means: Athena reads it as going against the current (ἀντί + ῥέω): the strength to swim against illusion and injustice.

values.name: Measure, the mean
values.means: The centre, which Athena calls the hearth of virtue, of divine nature and of eudaimonia.

values.name: Freedom
values.means: Not a memory but the present state of your existence; Athena finds eros inside the word.

values.name: Lasting fulfilment
values.means: An unshakeable fullness that depends on no condition: your inner flame, the δαίμων, touching its own good nature.

values.name: Love that unites
values.means: The force that makes the many into one universe; knowing yourself as it is, for Athena, the cure for separateness.

values.name: Eros
values.means: A current that carries you towards union and freedom: the beginning of philosophy, never attachment or obsession.

values.name: Healthy shame
values.means: The restraint felt before a wrong act: justice regulating itself within you.

values.name: Truth
values.means: Un-forgetting: a state, not a list of propositions; truth does not come to you, you come to it.

values.name: Beauty
values.means: Where the divine shows its wonder in the visible world, as Greek art’s devotion to symmetry and harmony shows.

values.name: The common logos
values.means: One and common to all (ξυνός): the consciousness that observes, and our power to judge just from unjust.

values.name: Education of the soul
values.means: Not diplomas but the art of turning the soul’s whole eye from outside to inside.

questions: Take the first of your five. Name one choice this week where it decided what you did, and one where something else decided instead.
Which of your five is least present in how you live now? Name one thing you could do this week to give it room.
